ai.description: The Adi Cascade Frog is a small amphibian with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale belly. It features prominent toe discs and distinct skin ridges, characteristic of its fast-flowing stream habitat.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops adicola* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, light-colored or white upper lip stripe that contrasts sharply against its dark snout.
ai.habitat: The Adi Cascade Frog inhabits high-altitude, fast-flowing rocky streams within primary subtropical evergreen forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically above 1,000m.
ai.behavior: The Adi Cascade Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops adicola* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 300–400 eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops adicola* is endemic to the East Siang district of Arunachal Pradesh, India, inhabiting high-elevation rocky streams within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The Adi Cascade Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, insect-like chirps that cut through the constant roar of its fast-flowing mountain stream habitat.
